title: Evaluation of indirect methods for the estimation of reference intervals
summary:
Reference intervals are essential for the clinical interpretation of laboratory test results and typically represent 95% of values obtained from healthy individuals. Reference limits, as indicated in textbooks or by manufacturers, must be verified by medical laboratories and regularly reviewed prior to application in routine clinical practice. Given the substantial effort entailed in recruiting at least 120 healthy subjects and conducting the requisite measurements using direct methods, indirect methods, which employ mathematical algorithms to verify reference limits from routine data, are increasingly becoming the focus of research interest. However, the most precise and robust estimate for a given application remains unclear.
The objective of the present project is to utilise a range of laboratory parameters as exemplars for the purpose of comparing the results of reference interval estimates derived from five indirect methods, based on data from multiple laboratories.
The five indirect methods are then applied to the respective data sets using an R script. The upper and lower reference limits for each laboratory, as well as the corresponding permissible measurement uncertainties, are then compiled and compared both with one another and against reference intervals from the literature.
conditions: Retrospective analysis of routine clinical laboratory data. No selection is made based on specific diseases.

interventions.name: A retrospective analysis of measurement results for seven laboratory parameters (potassium, alkaline phosphatase, gamma-GT, albumin, creatinine, enzymatic creatinine)  from all patients whose blood samples were analyzed in the participating laboratories over a period of at least one year.
